clue.text: Spring shoot

definitions.meaning: to spring up is to start growing, as a seed does
a shoot is a young growth coming up from a plant

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from new plant growth: the verb is to begin growing, the noun is the young stem itself.

clue.text: All the same, this suits a lot of people

definitions.text: this suits a lot of people
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: an outfit (suit) worn identically by many people, such as soldiers or schoolchildren

explanation.definitionFit: Identical throughout is the adjective; the noun is standard dress worn by every member of a group.

clue.text: Note union's shilly-shallying

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale
a union is an alliance; the 's is just a link

explanation.surface: A memo about a trade union dithering over its decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallying, or toying with something without commitment, is a form of dithering.

clue.text: Start serving 10 for the band

indicators.note: the start of the word serving is its opening letter

parts.note: the answer to 10 across is offal, and tripe is a kind of offal

explanation.surface: Kick off a meal by dishing up offal for a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to another clue's answer (OFFAL); TRIPE is an example of it, stomach lining sold as meat in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a band of colour, a strip running across a surface.

clue.text: Resistance noticed when capital is required

parts.note: armed resistance or fighting can be called war
saw means noticed

explanation.surface: Wartime partisans spotted something when the city was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Bias is not commonly an indication of militancy

parts.note: a warp is a bias or twist in outlook
ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: Prejudice, spoken carelessly, reveals a warlike streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Face paint worn before battle shows readiness to fight, hence a sign of aggressive intent.

clue.text: Show the right 21 round

parts.note: the answer to 21 down is ode, used here as it stands
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An exhibition of the correct answer encircled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills, so a type of show.

clue.text: Not thinking much of a sly bent developer

indicators.note: a developer reshapes things, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Being dismissive of a crafty, crooked property builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not thinking much of' reads as disapproval; the definition is the first three words, with 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something absently means doing it with the mind elsewhere, not paying attention.

clue.text: Hangers for underwear that's about the end!

indicators.note: the word for underwear goes around the other piece, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: pants is British for underpants

explanation.surface: Coat-hangers for knickers would be the last straw!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangers' suggests clothes-hangers, but it means things that hang down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are ornaments that hang from a chain or ceiling, things suspended.

clue.text: Dunderhead bearing in bread which is most coarse

indicators.note: the head letter and the bearing go inside the bread word

parts.note: crust is the hard outer part of bread
the head of the word dunder is its first letter D
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A fool carrying a loaf, which is the roughest behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like a fool, but it is split as the head of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudest is the superlative of crude, meaning rough, vulgar or unrefined.

clue.text: Sort of meat not available to a novice

parts.note: an item off the menu is not available
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A dish that a beginner cook is not allowed to have.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible innards of an animal, a category of butcher's meat.

clue.text: Criticise backing a horse, being superior

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for criticise is read backwards

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Panning someone for putting money on a horse, while acting superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like betting on the horse, but it turns RAP into PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, above all others in importance.

clue.text: A craft for a simpleton

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a craft or vessel

explanation.surface: A boat built for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, a dolt.

clue.text: Retraces moves and causes domestic rows

indicators.note: the letters of the word move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone retracing their steps and stirring up family arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels (rhyming with cows), but here it means lines of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Terraces are rows of joined houses, a common British form of housing.

clue.text: The point of a record-player

parts.note: the sharp tip on a turntable arm that runs in the groove; 'point' also suggests purpose

explanation.definitionFit: A stylus with a sharp tip reads the groove of a gramophone disc.

clue.text: See about a stern resolution in serious fashion

indicators.note: the see goes around the other letters, about meaning surrounding

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat (see) of a bishop

indicators.note: a resolution is a reworking or settling, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: Look over a harsh decision with grave intent.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is the crossword's favourite one.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means sincerely and with deep seriousness of purpose.

clue.text: Many with black look are charming and courteous

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
ebon is a poetic word for black
an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A crowd with dark expressions turn out to be pleasant and polite.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a suave, confident and well-mannered person.

clue.text: Give voice about public transport

parts.note: C, circa, means about
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Complain out loud about the buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out is to call aloud, to utter a sound.

clue.text: Being a little upset, Green tersely answers and goes in again

indicators.note: only a little of the words Green tersely is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Somewhat annoyed, a curt Mr Green replies and comes back into the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into a place is to make a second entry.

clue.text: Some Greeks get a weekly let, ter from Greece

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Greeks receive a weekly post from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: The French understand a person only renting property

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: Grasping the French view of a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, a tenant rather than an owner.

clue.text: Poetry due to be heard

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, so what we hear stands for a word of the same sound

parts.note: owed means due, as a debt

explanation.surface: Verse that is owed a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, a form of verse.

clue.text: 28 has to remain outside, it's ruled

indicators.note: the word for remain stays outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: to lie is to remain in a place, as in lie low
the answer to 28 across is steer, a young bullock, and neat is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay out of the way says it has been decided.
explanation.walkthrough: '28' refers to the answer to 28 across, a young bullock; NEAT is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate means marked with lines, as ruled paper is.

clue.text: To keep sounding a relative going inside can be discouraging

indicators.note: the relative is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to ding is to keep ringing, like a bell
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Constant ringing while an aunt comes in might be off-putting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something daunting is intimidating enough to sap one's resolve.

clue.text: A carnival on in NE Spain

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity carnival

explanation.surface: A festival held in north-eastern Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is the annual fund-raising festival run by British university students.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon is a region and former kingdom in the north-east of Spain.

clue.text: A very pleasant place for fish study

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A lovely spot to read up on fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden, as in the Garden of Eden, stands for a delightful spot.

clue.text: A rival read a number and turned a colour

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
ten is a number

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A competitor read out a figure and went red.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a competitor challenging for a title.

clue.text: Man races round reversing car and a homily results!

indicators.note: the races go round the other piece

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: reversing means the word car is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver backs a car around a racetrack, and a sermon follows!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man races' looks like a man racing, but it is the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often moral or religious, much like a sermon.

clue.text: Guide always to be seen at a holy man's side

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A guide who is always beside a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct or guide a course.

clue.text: Scoundrel joining state body

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A rogue joining a government body.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Game to take a course, receiving grant

indicators.note: the course word takes in the grant word

parts.note: a route is a course
to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: A student taking a course while living on a grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game with a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Not charged for rags-it appears wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Free old clothes, it seems, is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge.
